recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Visualization and Creating Your Own Path", "body": "Brandon described his creative process as writing down short and long term goals, then feeling as though he had already achieved them and imagining the results in his head. He credited his upbringing, saying his mother and stepdad met at a metaphysical school that taught Reiki and other healing arts, and that his parents told him college was never a necessity. Brandon explained that he started full time as an artist with little formal training, then added about 120 credit hours of art classes and specialized jewelry workshops over roughly eight years."}, {"title": "Electroforming and Energy in Metaphysical Jewelry", "body": "Brandon walked the show through Third Eye Jewelry, explaining that electroforming used chemistry and electricity to grow copper around objects such as honeycomb from his own beehive and crystals. He said he liked the science behind it and encouraged kids to stay curious about it. Brandon described a set of knives with teeth on the handle, saying their message was that energy is a full circle, so anyone who dealt damage would take some in return. Chance added that copper was good for circulation."}, {"title": "Selling Without Tricks and Pricing Custom Work", "body": "Brandon said he had always been outgoing and never liked pushing sales, preferring to tell booth visitors to touch the pieces and pick things up. He explained that most of his sales and buzz came through Instagram and Facebook, and that he often did not post a piece until it sold. On custom orders, Brandon said he only accepted ideas he found interesting and had time for, and that good custom work was expensive. Chance argued that clients paid for the experience behind the skill, not only the hours."}, {"title": "Dean on Making Music and Streaming Platforms", "body": "Dean introduced himself as a musician who played guitar, bass, didgeridoo, piano, and sang, and who played drums on a keyboard live. He said he made music because it gave him something that never ended, and that he stockpiled songs so a quiet release stretch caused less stress. Bandcamp came up as the best way to support him, and Dean said a monthly membership there cost 4.19 dollars, while he complained that SoundCloud charged him a fee before he could earn anything. He also described a new album and his Lucid TV videos."}, {"title": "NFTs, Art Basel, and Airship Banter", "body": "Dean said he and Brandon planned to join the NFT wave, calling NFTs not a real thing but still worth something because people believed they were. He described seeing an immersive 3D piece at Art Basel in Miami, projected on a giant curved LED wall and viewed with simple 3D glasses, as the most incredible visual experience of his life. Later the group joked about a mock rock pile documentary, talked about a trip to Egypt and the size of the pyramid blocks, and imagined an airship tour paid for with NFT money."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Brandon Arnold and Dean McDonnell are psychedelic creators from St. Louis. Brandon's Third Eye Jewelry blends futuristic vibes with metaphysical intent, using many natural materials (super heady). Dean is the mastermind behind LuSiD, an ever shifting audio-visual experience spanning far beyond conventional genres or expectations (he's a one-man band).
